memo.verdict: Progress to Early-Stage. Neutral on the shares at EUR 44.05, bullish on the business. Entry discipline: the case clears the framework's 20% bar on the modal path below about EUR 39 on the eighteen-month horizon (EUR 38.8) and below about EUR 46 on the three-year horizon (EUR 45.7); at EUR 44.05 the three-year clears and the eighteen-month does not. Conviction a working hypothesis (medium-low), because the return rests on a 50/50 multiple blend and a drop-through modelled by us. Gate line: management C, business quality C, predictability C, trackability B; no D or F, so not parked. Park trigger named: either multiple condition failing at the FY2026 results (around 1 April 2027), or H2 2026 openings missing the 476 floor so that 'No deceleration' moves and an eighth scoped attribute goes to D or F, making the combination red flag present.
case: Thesis: Fastned is a demand-inflection case with a proven operating-leverage engine inside it; the engine is proven, the balance sheet is thin, the price is early. At EUR 44.05 the shares already pay 48x a consensus-mean 24-month-forward EPS of EUR 0.9113 for earnings that only begin in FY2028, so the three-year return clears the bar and the eighteen-month does not.

1. The external change is structural, sector-wide and policy-backed, and reaches the company faster than the fleet grows. European battery-electric registrations +38% in H1 2026 and +51.1% in July 2026; fleet past 11 million; penetration Germany 24.8% from 17.7%, France 28.2% from 17.6%, UK 25.0% from 21.6%, Netherlands 36.5% from 35.0% despite registrations -34.3% on the company-car tax cliff. AFIR (pools every 60 km on TEN-T, 400 kW by 2025, 600 kW by 2027, mandatory ad-hoc payment above 50 kW), the kept EU 2035 target, German incentives up to EUR 6,000 and the March 2026 Düsseldorf ruling on open Autobahn tenders give visibility beyond two years. Fastned's energy delivered +38% in H1 2026, +44% in Q2; organic volume at existing stations +25.1% against weighted fleet growth of 3% on the company's measure: share of a growing pool, not only riding it. Conceded: part of the Q2 acceleration from 32% to 44% was the spring 2026 fuel-price spike of 15% to 20%; reversible; treated as cyclical throughout. 70% to 80% of charging is at home, which bounds the share of fleet energy a highway network can take, not the growth of the fleet.

2. The internal change is scale-up discipline, secondary but real. No chief-executive change. Strategy moved to Build-Grow-Optimize: selective tenders on return hurdles, decentralised country management across nine markets, B2C and B2B conversion (Gold membership about 15,000; B2B charge card with 36 fleets, +174% since year-end 2025), five OEM navigation integrations, urban joint ventures (Fast Places with Transport for London, 25 hubs by 2030). Standards: central procurement over about EUR 20m of indirect spend, zero-based budgeting, permits +89%, a 15-week on-site build; governance standards did not move. Funding in kind: the EUR 200m green bank facility beside EUR 337m of retail bonds and equity. Guidance raised once (13 August 2026, margin 35% to 40% to about 45%) after cuts in 2024 and January 2025, both grid-driven; sell-side FY2026 operational EBITDA +22% Jefferies (to EUR 82m), EUR 70m to EUR 81m ING, IFRS EBITDA +25% Deutsche Bank.
counter_case: The strongest case against is the "false friend" profile updated for the H1 2026 print: a network scaling superficially while returns dilute, dressed up by two artefacts and a thin market. The volume surge is a fuel-price artefact: pump prices rose 15% to 20% in spring 2026 and growth went from 32% to 44% in one quarter, with ING and Deutsche Bank expecting normalisation and ING having measured Q1 2026 organic growth (+21%) below penetration growth (+24%), implying share loss. The margin surge is an e-credit artefact: credit prices doubled in Germany, France and Belgium; Renewable Energy Units were EUR 13.2m of FY2025 revenue at near-100% margin; EUR 5.1m was deferred in H1 2026; e-credit scheme changes are the single largest margin risk and are political and unpredictable. The network's 13% average utilisation against 38% at the top five says every added site dilutes returns and the 1,000-station push adds the worst sites last; the 19% station return on invested capital is pre-tax, before central costs, at the average site, with the marginal site undisclosed, and new countries start below break-even with Spain's grid lead times over three years and 13,700 inactive Spanish points. The Dutch motorway share of over 60% cannot survive the 2028 to 2036 concession roll under rules that prohibit adjacent sites and cap local share at 50%; the draft auction law is unfinalised; impairment up to EUR 15m. Net debt EUR 369m is 15.5x FY2026 forecast operational EBITDA; EUR 337m of retail bonds must roll; consensus equity falls to EUR 58.5m against EUR 640m of debt by FY2028; a 7.5x debt-to-equity covenant has unquantified terms; FY2027 consensus free cash flow is the trough at EUR -127m, which may bring the equity question forward; the hedge cover falls to 25% to 35% in FY2027; interest already takes 42% of FY2025 operational EBITDA; there is no room for a miss. The company has cut station targets in two of the last three years, both on grid; H2 2026 needs 42 to 72 openings after 20 in Q2; the finance chair is an interim during the largest funding programme in the company's history; internal-control deficiencies are acknowledged; EUR 4.3m of staff costs were capitalised against a peer median of zero; there are three alternative performance measures and no quarterly EBITDA or pricing disclosure; the same half-year reads as EUR 37.4m, EUR 15.9m, EUR 13.7m or EUR -13.0m. The outside holder has no vote: the FAST foundation holds 100% of the votes and refuses proxies, management-board terms are indefinite, and the board puts the mission before short-term profit by its own statement. The shares doubled in six months on one half-year print and an oil shock, in a stock trading EUR 2m to EUR 4m a day with a 24% free float, to 48x an EPS figure that six of seven brokers put below the mean; a thin market can de-rate on as little as it re-rated. At 20x the 24-month-forward EPS the shares are EUR 18.2 (-59%); at the sector median EUR 15.9 (-64%); on an enterprise-value footing at 12x FY2027 IFRS EBITDA about EUR 21 (-52%) and at 10x about EUR 14 (-68%); Jefferies' own downside is EUR 15 and worst case EUR 10. The framework's own caution applies in full: EPS growth above 40% very likely returns to base rates and sentiment is too naive on that risk; a 'Pret sandwich' is forming; seven scoped attributes already sit at D or F, one short of the combination red flag; the broad-mediocrity share is at the top of the D band; the cockroach pattern is forming on one actual problem (Q2 openings) and one probable (the fuel kicker fading). On this reading the modal return is negative, the fit is a cyclical surge rather than a demand inflection, and a crisp mechanism on a fragile balance sheet at a full price is a case to park, not to progress.

What the record concedes: the e-credit dependence is real and the single largest margin risk; the fuel-price component of Q2 2026 is real and reversible; the leverage is at the limit and an equity raise is in our path and not the brokers'; the Dutch concession roll is a dated erosion of the best asset; the governance is an outlier we would not design; the multiple will fall; at EUR 44.05 the eighteen-month return does not clear the bar on the modal path and is a loss on the adverse drop-through.
triggers: - The two conditions that decide the multiple, tested at the FY2026 results around 1 April 2027: full-year FY2026 and FY2027 operational EBITDA margins at or above 45% on charging revenue; organic volume growth at or above 20% through FY2027. Either failing moves the cleared branch out and the Thesis to C.

- Organic volume growth as the fuel-price kicker fades: confirm above 20%; Alarm below 15% for two quarters with crude below EUR 70 a barrel; Invalidate below 10% with crude under EUR 70 for six months.

- Station openings: Q3 2026 update (October 2026) and Q4 2026 update (January 2027) with the year-end count against 476 to 506 and the first test of 70 to 100; FY2026 below 476 takes our path down a notch, above 500 takes it up; a third grid-driven cut is an Alarm.

- Funding: the next retail-bond campaign and its roll-over rate (Alarm: a campaign that fails to fill; roll-over below 50%); bank facility drawdowns; the timing and size of an equity raise (our modal about EUR 120m, about 15%; Invalidate: a raise above 25%).
- E-credits: scheme announcements in Germany, France, Belgium or the Netherlands; quote prices; gross profit per kWh (Invalidate below EUR 0.45; a 50% price fall).
- The Dutch highway-permit auction law's final terms (residual value, site criteria, the 50% cap) and the 2028 concession expiries.
